A.explanation: Both the driving force and total resistive forces act on the same car, so they are balanced forces on one body, not an action-reaction pair on two bodies.

B.explanation: The gravitational attraction of Earth on Moon and of Moon on Earth are the same type of force acting on two different bodies in opposite directions.

C.explanation: Both weight and support force act on the same block, so although equal in magnitude when at rest, they are not a Newton third law pair.

D.explanation: Both lift and weight act on the same aeroplane and are different types of force, so they cannot be a Newton third law action-reaction pair.

hints: Look at which object each arrow acts on in diagrams A, C and D compared with the Earth-Moon diagram.
Recall a Newton third law pair must be the same type of force, opposite in direction, and act on two different interacting bodies.
Check which pair shows two bodies pulling on each other, rather than two equal forces balancing on one car, block or aeroplane.
walkthrough: State the Newton third law test: if body X exerts a force on body Y, then body Y exerts an equal and opposite force of the same type on body X, so the two forces must be on different bodies.
In A, driving force and total resistive forces both act on the car. In C, support force and weight both act on the block. In D, lift and weight both act on the aeroplane.
Equal and opposite forces on the same object show balance or equilibrium, not a third law pair, so A, C and D fail the two-bodies test.
In B, one arrow is Earth pulling the Moon and the other arrow is Moon pulling the Earth. They are both gravitational attraction, equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
That matches the action-reaction description exactly. This is option B.
